justification: The prompt says 'Carlos needs an email from us that 3C is clear so leasing can start today.' Carlos is the primary recipient of the leasing hand-off. Gmail in StarPM is draft-only; there is no send action.
evidence: Look for a Gmail draft-create call with the to parameter containing carlos.mendez@starpm.com. Confirm the tool returned a success response with a draft id.

justification: The prompt says 'Copy Brooke so she knows the loop closed on 3C.' Brooke needs to be cc'd on the hand-off so she sees the loop closure without being the primary recipient.
evidence: Check the cc parameter of the Gmail draft-create call for brooke.phillips@starpm.com. A draft that omits Brooke from cc, or that places her in to instead of cc, fails this rubric.

title: The Agent's Gmail draft to Carlos threads under Brooke's 6/18 closeout package thread (Gmail thread b8e4d0a3f2c5b9e7 via replyToMessageId d0e6f2c5b4a70b19).

title: The Agent creates a calendar event on Jaime Salinas's primary calendar (jaime.salinas@starpm.com) for a Friday morning 3C spot-check reminder.
justification: The prompt says 'set me a reminder for Friday morning to spot-check 3C's fridge and oven interiors again.' The reminder is on Jaime's own calendar so it fires for Jaime, not for another team member.
evidence: Look for a calendar event-create call for a Friday morning 3C spot-check reminder. The event must land on Jaime Salinas's primary calendar, satisfied either by an explicit calendarId parameter equal to jaime.salinas@starpm.com OR by the tool result confirming creator.email is jaime.salinas@starpm.com with self:true (which indicates the event was created on the operating user's primary calendar). Confirm the tool returned a success response with an event id. A cron-scheduler call such as CronCreate instead of create_event fails this rubric because no calendar event is created.

title: The Agent's calendar reminder lands on Friday 2026-07-03 in the morning window (between 07:00 and 11:00 America/Chicago).
justification: The prompt says 'set me a reminder for Friday morning ... before whichever tour hits earliest.' Today is Wednesday 2026-07-01; the next Friday is 2026-07-03. The reminder must fire before whichever tour hits earliest, so a morning-window landing on that specific Friday is required. The window ends at 11:00 CT to sit before typical showing hours starting at noon or later.
evidence: Check the startTime and endTime parameters of the calendar event-create call. The startTime must fall on 2026-07-03 between 07:00 and 11:00 in America/Chicago (or the equivalent -05:00 offset). A reminder on any other date, or later in the day than 11:00 CT, fails this rubric.

evidence: Check the summary parameter of the calendar event-create call for a reference to Las Vistas 3C. A generic 'reminder' or 'follow-up' summary that omits the unit fails this rubric, even if the unit is buried in the description.
